tools.description: Start work in one call: files a new task (or takes an existing one with task_id), plans its steps, marks it in progress and starts the first step. tools.name: taskhold_list
tools.description: List top-level tasks, one line each, grouped by status. Pass project to see one repo's work. Each line has status, title, steps done, progress and id; steps aren't listed (taskhold_get shows them). An unknown project name returns no tasks and is not created.

tools.name: taskhold_get
tools.description: Get one task with its full description, steps (subtasks), progress, labels and the latest notes. tools.description: Get the task in progress (in this project when you pass project), with its steps and the next one to do. Call this at the start of a session. tools.name: taskhold_search
tools.description: Search tasks and steps by text in the title or description (case-insensitive, up to 100 tasks scanned). Returns matching lines grouped by status, with ids (a step names the task it belongs to), or a line saying nothing matched.

tools.name: taskhold_create
tools.description: File work for later: a bug, a refactor, a follow-up you aren't doing now (it lands in To Do). To file and start work at once, use taskhold_begin. tools.description: Move the person's progress bar during a long step or a task without steps: percent, or current and total (e.g. 12 of 40 files), plus a short message about what's happening now. On a task with steps, the steps drive the bar: numbers you send for the task go to its running step. Call at milestones, ev

tools.description: Create a task from a TODO comment in code, keeping the file path and line number (label todo-from-code plus any labels you pass; priority as in taskhold_create; use taskhold_create for anything else). Returns the new task with its id and code location. Fails at the account's task ceiling or on an in

tools.description: Mark a task or step in progress when you begin it. Starting a step also starts its task. For new work, taskhold_begin files, plans and starts in one call. Returns the id, status and the next step's id when it has steps. Safe to repeat; it also resumes a blocked or done task. An unknown task_id fails

tools.description: Mark a task or step done, with a summary of what you did and, optionally, a structured outcome: files changed (with +/- line counts), checks run (pass/fail/skip), links (PR, commit, branch, deploy, doc), follow-up task ids, risks and how the person can verify it. tools.name: taskhold_block
tools.description: Mark a task (or step) blocked when you can't continue without the person (a decision, missing info, access). Returns the question and the exact taskhold_updates call to wait with. Write the reason as one question they can answer from the board in a line, e.g. "Decide: drop the legacy column or keep

tools.name: taskhold_unblock
tools.description: Move a blocked task back to todo once the blocker is resolved (taskhold_start resumes it directly). Returns the task with status todo. A task that isn't blocked is left as it is and the reply says its status; an unknown task_id fails with "Task not found".

tools.name: taskhold_update
tools.description: Update a task's title, description, priority or project. Only fields you pass change; status goes through taskhold_start, taskhold_complete and taskhold_block. Returns the task as it is now. Fails on an unknown task_id, a project_id that doesn't exist (pass project by name instead) or an invalid pro

tools.name: taskhold_add_note
tools.description: Add a note to a task: findings, decisions, what you tried. The person reads these. Notes are append-only and shown oldest first (taskhold_get shows the latest 10). Returns a one-line confirmation; an unknown task_id fails with "Task not found".

tools.name: taskhold_set_priority
tools.description: Change a task's priority. Returns the task title and new priority; an unknown task_id fails with "Task not found".

tools.name: taskhold_updates
tools.description: What the person changed since you last looked: replies (notes), new tasks, priority changes, unblocks. Call when you resume, between steps, and after blocking (with wait, to hold until the reply lands). Pass the cursor from the previous call (or from taskhold_begin / taskhold_block) as since. Your o

tools.name: taskhold_list_projects
tools.description: List projects with their open work, one line each. You rarely need this: every tool takes project as a name. Each line has the name, open counts (working, blocked, todo) and id.

tools.name: taskhold_create_project
tools.description: Create a project (a group of tasks, usually one per repo). Optional: any tool that takes project creates it on first use. Returns the existing project if one has this name (case-insensitive), without changing it: the reply says if your description or color wasn't applied (taskhold_update_project cha

tools.name: taskhold_update_project
tools.description: Change a project's name, description or color. Only fields you pass change. Returns the project as it is now. Fails on an unknown project (it is never created here), on a name another project already has, or with nothing to change.

tools.name: taskhold_list_labels
tools.description: List the account's labels, one name per line. Labels are created by passing them to taskhold_create or taskhold_begin.

tools.name: taskhold_get_summary
tools.description: Task counts by status, priority and who added them (human or agent). Returns the total and one list per grouping; counts top-level tasks only, not steps.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: taskhold_complete · Private data: taskhold_begin, taskhold_get, taskhold_create, taskhold_progress, taskhold_create_from_todo, taskhold_start, taskhold_complete · Public sink: taskhold_progress · Destructive: taskhold_complete, taskhold_block.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: taskhold_complete · Private data: taskhold_begin, taskhold_get, taskhold_create, taskhold_progress, taskhold_create_from_todo, taskhold_start, taskhold_complete · Public sink: taskhold_progress · Destructive: taskhold_complete, taskhold_block

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
